prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1243; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim received by phone from the insured driver following a low-speed head-on collision at an intersection. Insured reports the other vehicle crossed the center line while turning. Insured states both vehicles were driven away from the scene. Police report requested from the local department.

Entry 2: Spoke with the other driver, who reports neck and back strain after the impact and has visited an urgent care clinic. Claimant is not represented by an attorney and says they are handling the matter directly. Explained the claims process and the coverage questions still under review. Requested medical records and treatment notes with a signed authorization.

Entry 3: Reviewed photos submitted by both drivers. Front bumper damage on both vehicles is consistent with a low-speed impact, with no airbag deployment reported. Estimate requested from the preferred repair shop for the insured vehicle. Left a voicemail for the claimant asking for a callback about the rental vehicle.

Entry 4: Claimant returned the call and described ongoing stiffness in the neck and lower back, with headaches on some mornings. Advised that the claim file will remain open pending the medical records. Discussed rental car coverage limits and provided a copy of the claim number and adjuster contact information in writing.

Entry 5: Received the police report, which lists the other driver as cited for failure to maintain lane. Medical records from the clinic have arrived and show a diagnosis of cervical and lumbar strain with a follow-up recommended with a physical therapist. Reserves reviewed and updated. Scheduled a follow-up call with the claimant for next week to confirm physical therapy progress.
